title: US reverses course on Britain's testing of AI models, Telegraph says
source_used: Reuters text as carried by The Hindu (Reuters page returned HTTP 401); context from Startup Fortune
key_facts: The Telegraph reported on Sunday 11 Oct 2026 that American AI developers can give the British government early access to AI models for safety testing without running afoul of the Trump administration.
The administration has reversed a decision that asked developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic not to share new models with Britain's AI Security Institute before release.
Reuters calls the change a softer stance by the Trump administration on international AI safety efforts.
Spokespersons for Trump, OpenAI and Anthropic did not immediately respond to Reuters.
Britain's AI Security Institute, set up after the 2023 AI safety summit, tests the most advanced AI models for capabilities and risk of misuse.
Trump's newly launched AI task force said on Friday that developers must report security incidents with their AI models.

Startup Fortune (summarising the Telegraph) adds that the pause was ordered on 24 Sep 2026 by the White House Office of the National Cyber Director and lasted 17 days; this detail is single-source and not used in the entry.
quote_evidence: The Trump administration has reversed a decision that requested developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic not to share new AI models with Britain's AI Security Institute before release, the newspaper said.

The change signals a softer stance by the Trump administration on international AI safety efforts, giving US developers greater latitude to cooperate with Britain as policymakers grapple with how to oversee the increasingly powerful technology.
His newly launched AI task force said on Friday developers must report security incidents with their AI models.
why_it_matters_hint: British government testers can again see leading US models before release, per one newspaper's report that the White House and companies had not yet commented on.
notes: Reuters original blocked (HTTP 401). Reuters text read on The Hindu; context from Startup Fortune. The Telegraph original was not opened. White House and companies had not commented when Reuters filed.
